evidence: All checks were run on the frozen snapshot .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r1/task. (1) TOML: Python 3 tomllib loaded task.toml (schema_version, artifacts, task, metadata, agent, environment, verifier), tests/scoring.toml (gates render/constraints 0.0; weights functional 0.6, polish 0.2, visual 0.2; floor functional 0.05; byte-identical to the template) and all five judge.toml files with no error. (2) Real loader: in a throwaway container (docker run --rm --network none, tests mounted read-only, image cw-editor-verifier:current with harbor-rewardkit 0.1.7, the version tests/Dockerfile pins), rewardkit.runner.discover() built every judge. gates/constraints: AgentJudge, batched, 600 s, 1 criterion, all_pass. gates/render: AgentJudge, batched, 600 s, 1 criterion, all_pass. scored/functional: AgentJudge, individual, 520 s, 17 criteria, weighted_mean. scored/polish: batched, 900 s, 5 criteria. scored/visual: batched, 900 s, 4 Likert criteria. rewardkit 0.1.7 models.py:142 declares JudgeMode = Literal['batched','individual'], so the non-template mode = 'individual' is valid. (3) Shell: bash -n returned 0 for tests/test.sh and solution/solve.sh, and both start with #!/bin/bash. A byte scan of every file in the task found no CR byte and no UTF-8 BOM. (4) Prompts: every prompt.md has exactly one {app_context} and one {criteria} placeholder and no other braces. tests/app_context.md has no braces, so the substitution at test.sh lines 195-201 and later template formatting cannot raise KeyError or IndexError. (5) Seed and entry: environment/assets/kittle.json and solution/app/seed/kittle.json parse as JSON and are byte-identical (sha256 42ab8b97...). package.json parses. node --check (v24.19.0) passes server.js and public/app.js. Python compile() passes tests/tools/score.py and restart_mcp.py. These and test.sh, tests/Dockerfile, .dockerignore and environment/Dockerfile are byte-identical to the template. (6) Would run: solve.sh copies app/ to /app. test.sh line 68 requires /app/server.js and line 104 launches it with env -i, NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules, PORT=3000, DB_PATH and uid 65534. server.js requires only express and better-sqlite3, which environment/Dockerfile installs globally at the same pinned versions. It listens on PORT/0.0.0.0 (line 519), serves /api/health (line 42), which test.sh probes, and falls back to /assets/kittle.json for the seed (line 29). integration.md line 3 states the same server.js/3000/NODE_PATH/DB_PATH contract publicly. Measured boot: the raw-evidence index binds golden-run.log (sha256 9930f70d..., verified) to source hashes that I recomputed and that match the frozen bytes (server.js a8a4a561..., app.js 3875be4e..., solve.sh f7c17a01..., seed 42ab8b97...). That log shows the frozen solve.sh install, two boots ('Kittle & Rowe matter chat on port 3000' at start and after restart) under the test.sh-style env -i/setpriv launch (run_golden.sh line 20), and exit 0. Scope limits: the log covers boot and the scripted functional checks only. It is not a configured judge run or Oracle score, and this row does not claim one. A full configured verifier run belongs to the separate runtime records. Counterexample attempts: (a) A broken app that could pass this row: none applies, because this row covers the task files, not agent output; an agent app missing /app/server.js exits with reward 0 at test.sh line 68, as the template intends. (b) A conforming alternative that could fail: an agent that follows integration.md (server.js, port 3000, global modules via NODE_PATH) is launched exactly that way, so I found no parse or launch path that would reject it.
